objectiveEnglish: Explain a wrong coffee and missing pastry politely in French.
focusFrench: Signaler une erreur avec je crois que ; opposer deux boissons avec pas ; dire qu'il me manque un article.
focusEnglish: Use je crois que to soften a correction, pas to contrast items, and il me manque for a missing item.

cards.note: Viennoiserie is the closest French category, not a literal equivalent.
For a woman, say la serveuse.

cards.targetFrench: Excusez-moi, je crois qu'il y a une erreur dans ma commande.
cards.supportEnglish: Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order.
cards.sourceSpanish: Disculpe, creo que hay un error con mi pedido.
cards.note: Use vous with one staff member.

cards.targetFrench: J'ai commandé un americano, pas un café au lait.
cards.supportEnglish: I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk.
cards.sourceSpanish: Pedí un café americano, no un café con leche.

cards.targetFrench: Pourriez-vous me l'échanger, s'il vous plaît ?
cards.supportEnglish: Can you change it for me, please?

cards.targetFrench: Pouvez-vous vérifier ma commande, s'il vous plaît ?
cards.supportEnglish: Can you check my order, please?

reader.targetFrench: J'arrive au comptoir et je commande un americano et une viennoiserie.
reader.supportEnglish: I get to the counter and order an americano and a pastry.
reader.sourceSpanish: Llego al mostrador y pido un café americano y un pan dulce.

reader.targetFrench: Puis le serveur me donne une tasse de café au lait.
reader.supportEnglish: Then the server gives me a cup of coffee with milk.
reader.sourceSpanish: Después, el mesero me da una taza de café con leche.

reader.targetFrench: Je vérifie mon sac et je vois qu'il n'y a pas de viennoiserie.
reader.supportEnglish: I check my bag and see that there is no pastry in it.
reader.sourceSpanish: Reviso mi bolsa y veo que no hay pan dulce.

reader.targetFrench: Je souris d'abord et je dis : « Excusez-moi, je crois qu'il y a une erreur dans ma commande. »
reader.supportEnglish: First, I smile and say: Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order.
reader.sourceSpanish: Primero, sonrío y digo: Disculpe, creo que hay un error con mi pedido.

reader.targetFrench: Puis j'explique : « J'ai commandé un americano, pas un café au lait. »
reader.supportEnglish: Then I explain: I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk.
reader.sourceSpanish: Luego explico: Pedí un café americano, no un café con leche.

reader.targetFrench: J'ajoute : « Il me manque une viennoiserie, et voici mon reçu. »
reader.supportEnglish: I also say: I am missing a pastry, and here is my receipt.
reader.sourceSpanish: También digo: Me falta un pan dulce, y aquí está mi recibo.

reader.targetFrench: Je demande : « Pourriez-vous me l'échanger, s'il vous plaît ? »
reader.supportEnglish: I ask: Can you change it for me, please?
reader.sourceSpanish: Pregunto: ¿Me lo puede cambiar, por favor?

reader.targetFrench: Le serveur dit : « Bien sûr, je vous apporte le café et la viennoiserie tout de suite. »
reader.supportEnglish: The server says: Of course, I will bring you the coffee and the pastry now.
reader.sourceSpanish: El mesero dice: Claro, ahora le traigo el café y el pan dulce.

forms.exampleFrench: Je commande un americano et une viennoiserie.
forms.exampleEnglish: I order an americano and a pastry.
forms.explanationEnglish: French splits pedir into two verbs. Commander means to order food or drink, which is the sense used here. Demander means to ask for something (Je demande l'addition). Commander is a regular -er verb with no stem change, so the Spanish e-to-i change does not carry over. Polite form: vous commandez.

forms.exampleFrench: Je vérifie mon sac, et il n'y a pas de viennoiserie.
forms.exampleEnglish: I check my bag and there is no pastry.
forms.explanationEnglish: Vérifier is the closest French verb for check. It is a regular -ier verb, so nous takes -ions (nous vérifions). Polite form: vous vérifiez.

forms.exampleFrench: Pouvez-vous me changer le café, s'il vous plaît ?
forms.exampleEnglish: Can you change the coffee for me, please?
forms.explanationEnglish: Changer is a regular -er verb. Nous changeons keeps the e so the g stays soft. Échanger (to exchange) is used in card 14 and Reader line 7 for changing the order item. Polite form: vous changez.

forms.exampleFrench: Je vous apporte le café et la viennoiserie tout de suite.
forms.exampleEnglish: I will bring you the coffee and the pastry now.
forms.explanationEnglish: Apporter means to bring. It is regular, so the irregular yo form of traer (traigo) does not carry over. Before a vowel, je becomes j'. Polite form: vous apportez.

forms.exampleFrench: D'abord je souris et je dis : « Excusez-moi. »
forms.exampleEnglish: First I smile and say: Excuse me.
forms.explanationEnglish: Dire means to say. It is irregular in French, so the forms do not follow the Spanish e-to-i pattern. Polite form: vous dites.

roles.englishDescription: You, the learner. You order breakfast for yourself, your wife, your son, and your mother-in-law, then repeat the order yourself to confirm who gets what, and ask for the check at the end.
The server who opens the exchange, takes your order, listens while you repeat it, confirms that everything is right, brings the food and, at the end, the check.

speaking.openingFrench: Bonjour ! Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?
objectivesEnglish: Open the order by saying you want to order for everyone.
Assign items to each person with pour moi, pour ma femme, pour mon fils, pour ma belle-mère, or pour elle.
Say 'without cheese' with sans for an exclusion.
Repeat the order yourself and ask the waiter to confirm who gets what.
Ask for the check at the end.

internalNotes.note: Source setting is pan dulce, a sweet-pastry term common in Mexican and US Spanish. The French gloss une viennoiserie is a cultural substitution (closest French category of baked goods), not a literal equivalent. The Mexican/US setting is noted here only and is not carried into the French lesson.

Corrected from old draft: 'Il manque' changed to 'Il me manque' to express I am missing; Reader line 3 'Je regarde' changed to 'Je vérifie' to match revisar; Reader line 8 'répond' changed to 'dit' to match source says. Old draft mode inputs listing all 16 items per mode were replaced by six authored modes.
The family-ordering scenario (wife, son, mother-in-law) comes from the speaking specification, not the pinned passage. Reader narration stays first-person je with no role substitution.
Pedir is split between commander (order food or drink, used here) and demander (ask for). Cambiar is mapped to changer, with échanger used in card 14 and Reader line 7.
